subject: Roadmap exceptions action capture and exec clarifications
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Roadmap exceptions action capture and exec clarifications

Hi team,

Thanks for a focused weekly sync this morning. I wanted to capture the follow-ups and flag two exec-level clarifications we need before the QBR pack is finalized for FinTechCo. Attaching the exceptions register and the current QBR ask tracker.

Quick summary of actions we agreed on:
- Marcus: confirm whether the model-variant fallback for low-memory hosts can be validated by EOD Tue (priority for FinTechCo runbook).
- Maya: update the QBR slide deck with the 99th percentile latency chart + cost delta; add a 1-slide summary for the suggested temporary SLA exception.
- Aditya: confirm whether we can approve a one-time SLA exception (30-day elevated availability commitment) pending infra mitigation.
- Lauren: own the QBR approval thread and coordinate with procurement for terms.

Exec clarifications we need (answer for QBR notes):
1) If we approve the temporary SLA exception, do we also commit to a short-term budget increase for burst capacity? (yes/no + ballpark $)
2) Are we comfortable shipping the quantization recommendation to FinTechCo as a mitigation inside the exception window? Any risk notes to call out?

Deadlines: please reply with tagged updates by 2027-05-03 18:00 PT so I can lock slides Monday evening.

Attachments: exceptions-register-20270502.xlsx, qbr-ask-tracker-20270502.pdf

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Roadmap exceptions action capture and exec clarifications

Thanks Soojin — quick status update:
- I ran a smoke validation on the fallback model-variant on Friday night. The variant reduces memory footprint by ~28% but shows a 6–8% increase in median latency on long sequences.
- I flagged two infra tasks that block canarying on the customer fleet: swapping the redis KV TTL config and a minor kernel upgrade on the older instances. I've attached infra-capacity-notes.txt with the checklist.

I can confirm feasibility by EOD Tue if infra can schedule the kernel upgrade early Monday. If not, we should call that out as "blocked" in the exceptions register and offer the quantization path as Plan B for the QBR.

On the exec questions: I recommend we approve the temporary SLA exception with the condition that we commit to a short burst capacity allocation (estimate below). Happy to sync with Aditya on the precise wording.

— Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

> On Sun, May 2, 2027 at 09:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Thanks for a focused weekly sync this morning...
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 12:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Roadmap exceptions action capture and exec clarifications

Adding my updates and linking the slide draft here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBRpack-FinTechCo

Planned changes for QBR slides:
- New slide: 99th percentile latency for FinTechCo traffic (baseline vs quantized variant).
- One-slide "risk & mitigations" for the temporary SLA exception (calls out increased tail latency risk and mitigation: prioritized cache warming + prefix KV caching).
- Callout for cost impact: preliminary estimate is +$7k/month for burst reserve (we should confirm with finance).

Question for Aditya: if we approve the exception, do we want to propose a self-serve toggle for FinTechCo to enable the fallback model during peak windows (so they can opt-in to the degraded-latency, lower-cost path)? That reduces blast radius since it's customer-controlled.

I'll update the tracker and mark "slide ready" once I add the charts (aiming for Mon morning).

— Maya
Sr. PM, Customer Solutions

> On Sun, May 2, 2027 at 11:04 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Thanks Soojin — quick status update...
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Kate Foster <kate@fintechco.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Roadmap exceptions action capture and exec clarifications

I can approve a one-time SLA exception contingent on the following being true by the start of the QBR window (May 15):
1) We commit to a measured burst capacity (est. $7k/month) to cover increased load while infra hardens.
2) We include an explicit rollback trigger: if 99th percentile latency regresses >15% for two consecutive days, exception is pulled.

If those are acceptable I'll sign off and Lauren can take that to procurement/FinTechCo.

Kate — looping you for visibility. If procurement needs a formal proposal, Lauren, can you draft the short amendment and point Kate to the exceptions register?

— Aditya
VP, Product

> On Sun, May 2, 2027 at 12:33 PM Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Adding my updates and linking the slide draft here...
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Kate Foster <kate@fintechco.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Roadmap exceptions action capture and exec clarifications

Thanks everyone — concise next steps from my side:
- I'll draft the proposed 30-day SLA exception amendment and send to Kate + procurement by EOD Mon. Doc will include the rollback trigger and burst-cost estimate ($7k/month).
- Marcus: please update the exceptions-register status column to "canary pending infra" if infra can't commit to the kernel upgrade by Monday.
- Maya: once slides are in Drive, I'll collate and produce the final QBR packet.
- Soojin: I'll own the final sign-off chain and share the signed amendment link (DocuSign stub) when ready.

Proposed meeting: Tue 2027-05-04 10:00 PT (30 min) — I'll send a calendar invite after I get Marcus's infra confirmation.

Attachments referenced in thread: exceptions-register-20270502.xlsx, qbr-ask-tracker-20270502.pdf, infra-capacity-notes.txt

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Growth
Redwood Inference
